what_it_does: Creates an automated system for generating multiple-choice exam questions directly from scientific papers to keep evaluation benchmarks up-to-date with rapidly evolving research. The system parses PDFs, extracts relevant content, generates questions, and evaluates how well smaller language models (1.1 to 14 billion parameters) can answer them. Demonstrates the approach on 22,000 papers in radiation and cancer biology, comparing whether retrieval-augmented generation (using paper passages) or reasoning-based retrieval (using the model's own reasoning steps) better helps smaller models learn domain-specific knowledge.
